title: Decompose legacy reliability regression checks
summary: Inventory and decompose the archived legacy desktop reliability monolith into focused, replacement-validated suites without changing production media behavior.
reason: The optional 6,602-line legacy harness is structurally unrunnable after the desktop-shell and pipeline layout migrations, yet it still contains unique safety assertions mixed with already-focused and obsolete coverage. A durable block map and replacement-first migration are required before any removal.
behavior_before: The archived legacy reliability script contains hundreds of static assertions, 50 PowerShell behavior harness calls, and embedded Python checks without a machine-readable block-to-replacement ledger. The whole script stops before assertions execute because it resolves removed paths.
behavior_after: Every logical legacy block is classified in the existing test-suite inventory authority with runnability, fixtures, production surfaces, focused-equivalence evidence, destination, and real-media requirements. Blocks are removed only after replacement or obsolescence evidence passes; focused reliability coverage remains runnable independently.
tests_added: FFmpeg progress parser cases in Invoke-FFmpegProgressChecks.ps1.
Inventory schema, exact-once mapping, anchor, removal-gate, and audit-manifest tests.
Native timeout and external-tool result/repro contracts in Invoke-NativeProcessCleanupChecks.ps1.
Pipeline event envelope round-trip in Invoke-LoggingJsonLineChecks.ps1.
manual_validation: BASELINE: broader 208-test desktop batch has one pre-existing snapshot expectation failure (audit_reports warning versus active), reproduced in isolation.
NOT REQUIRED: real-media validation because no production media behavior changed.
PASS: Local API lifecycle contract smoke (49 lifecycle tests and 2 HTTP shutdown tests).
PASS: PathBoundaryGuard and ScratchCopyIdentity preservation assessment suites.
PASS: ProgressStateTelemetry, LoggingJsonLine, AudioPolicy, FFmpegProgress, NativeProcessCleanup, and ToolLogLifecycle PowerShell suites.
PASS: Python inventory/audit and desktop process-control/local-API lifecycle tests.
PASS: inventory checker maps all 528 remaining assertion-bearing lines across 93 blocks exactly once.
rollback_plan: Restore each removed legacy block from this change's diff, revert its inventory disposition to active, and remove only the corresponding newly added focused assertions. Re-run the block-map validator and the affected focused suite before retrying a smaller tranche. Production source is not changed by this refactor.
notes:
Gate 1 was approved by the operator. Boundary register and validation ladder were read before edits. Ten blocks were removed only after focused replacements passed and evidence was recorded: LDRR-PS-002, LDRR-PS-003, LDRR-PS-004, LDRR-PS-017, LDRR-PS-018, LDRR-PS-019, LDRR-PS-020, LDRR-PS-021, LDRR-PS-022, and LDRR-PS-023. The script shrank from 6,602 to 6,033 lines (569 lines, 8.6%). The 18 embedded-Python blocks remain active and were conservatively reclassified unclear/preserve because a removed bootstrap path is not proof that similarly named current service behavior is obsolete. Source/scratch path and integrity blocks with incomplete focused equivalence also remain active. Real-media validation becomes required if later tranches change production source/scratch isolation, publish park/drain, subtitle conversion/OCR, audio routing, FFmpeg remux/encode output, or final placement. Unrelated dirty files, concurrent generated-context changes, and archived-packet movement are excluded. Existing overlapping edits in audit_checks.py, test_audit_checks.py, the Markdown inventory, and generated summaries were preserved.
Uses production audio choice registry and retains exact passthrough profile membership assertions.
Refreshed after focused audio policy assertions changed.
